analyses.method_selected: Customer segmentation + Pareto analysis on voluntary churn
analyses.method_reasoning: Statistical reason: H1 already established a channel-level effect at p<<0.001; segmentation surfaces whether the effect is uniform within paid_search or concentrated in sub-cohorts. Business reason: a retention investment is sized off the highest-impact sub-segment, not the channel average.
execution_steps: Group Q3 paid_search users by sub-channel (Google brand, Google non-brand, Bing, Facebook).
Compute voluntary churn rate per sub-channel; rank by absolute churned-user contribution.
Apply Pareto: identify the smallest set of sub-channels accounting for ≥80% of paid_search voluntary churn.

results.key_metric: Voluntary churn rate by paid_search sub-channel
results.value: Google non-brand: 41% • Bing: 35% • Facebook: 28% • Google brand: 18%
results.business_interpretation: Google non-brand alone produces 47% of the paid_search voluntary-churn volume. Two sub-channels (non-brand + Bing) cover 72% of it. A retention intervention narrowly targeted at non-brand could move the channel-level metric materially.

analyses.method_selected: Funnel analysis on first-30-day activation events
analyses.method_reasoning: Statistical reason: H2 showed a per-event-count odds ratio of 0.66 — but the actionable question is which events break the funnel. Funnel analysis attributes drop-off to specific steps. Business reason: product team needs to know which onboarding step to fix.
execution_steps: Define activation funnel: signup → first login → first feature_used → first weekly recurring event.
Compute step-level conversion rates for retained vs voluntary-churn cohorts.
Identify the step with the largest cohort-level drop differential.

results.key_metric: Step-level conversion gap between retained and voluntary-churn cohorts
results.value: first_feature_used step: retained 84% / churn 38% — gap of 46pp (largest in the funnel)
results.baseline_comparison: Other steps gap: signup→login = 8pp, login→feature_used = 46pp, feature_used→weekly = 18pp.
results.business_interpretation: The single biggest break is users logging in but never using a feature. Onboarding intervention should target the login-to-first-feature step — that is where the 65% engagement gap from H2 actually lives.

analyses.method_reasoning: Statistical reason: H3 supports a level-shift after 2025-07-15 but is UNDERPOWERED on the post-window. Decomposing the trend by plan_tier checks if the shift concentrates on a vulnerable tier (Phase 4 anomaly: starter 'first-bill cliff'). Business reason: pricing intervention is tier-specific.
execution_steps: Decompose weekly voluntary-churn series into trend + seasonal + residual using STL.
Repeat the decomposition per plan_tier (Starter, Pro, Enterprise).
Compare residuals around 2025-07-15 — the residual spike is the pricing effect after seasonality is removed.

results.baseline_comparison: Whole-base post-shift was +44%; tier breakdown shows Starter dominates.
results.business_interpretation: The pricing-change effect is overwhelmingly a Starter-tier phenomenon. This aligns with the Phase 4 'first-bill cliff' anomaly and points to price-sensitivity at the entry tier rather than a base-wide perception issue.

root_cause_chains.symptom: Paid_search users churn voluntarily at 31% vs organic at 14%.

proximate_cause.description: Paid_search users never reach first_feature_used (login→feature gap of 46pp vs retained users).
proximate_cause.evidence: Funnel analysis (SQ2): retained 84% reach first_feature_used vs 38% for voluntary-churn cohort. Logistic regression slope is steeper for paid_search (H4).

contributing_factor.description: Paid_search lands users on a generic activation flow that is not aligned with the search-intent they came from.
contributing_factor.evidence: Sub-channel breakdown: Google non-brand (highest intent-mismatch) has the highest voluntary churn at 41%; Google brand (high-intent) is the lowest at 18%.

root_cause.description: Onboarding flow is undifferentiated by acquisition intent — users with low-fit intent receive the same first-feature prompt as users with high-fit intent, so they bounce.
root_cause.evidence: Sub-channel × first_feature_used cross-tab: every 10-point increase in sub-channel intent-fit score correlates with a 5-point increase in first_feature_used completion (Pearson r = 0.71).
root_cause.data_needed_to_confirm: An A/B test comparing intent-segmented onboarding flow against the existing flow, measuring first_feature_used and 90-day voluntary churn.

proximate_cause.description: Starter-tier voluntary-churn residual spiked by +68% after the pricing change; Pro and Enterprise tiers were not meaningfully affected.

contributing_factor.description: Starter-tier users were already concentrated at the day-28 'first-bill cliff' in Phase 4.
contributing_factor.evidence: Phase 4 multivariate_pattern: Starter voluntary churn concentrates at days 28–35 (the first-bill window).

root_cause.description: The pricing change pushed Starter-tier first-bill totals over a perception threshold, converting an already-vulnerable cohort into churners at a higher rate.
root_cause.evidence: The post-shift effect is +68% in Starter tier and ~0% in Enterprise; the day-28 churn cluster from Phase 4 is the population that is uniquely sensitive to first-bill size.

segment_deep_dives.highest_impact_segment: Google non-brand (47% of paid_search voluntary churn volume)
segment_deep_dives.magnitude_in_segment: Voluntary churn = 41% (vs 14% organic baseline; absolute gap of 27pp)

segment_deep_dives.highest_impact_segment: Starter (largest n × largest base churn rate)
segment_deep_dives.magnitude_in_segment: OR per +1 log(events) = 0.61 in Starter vs 0.78 in Enterprise

impact_quantification.finding: Intent-segmented onboarding for paid_search (especially Google non-brand)
impact_quantification.opportunity_estimate: Closing 30% of the non-brand gap to organic would prevent ~810 churned users over a Q-window — equivalent to ~$1.2M ARR retained (assuming ARPU $1.5k).
impact_quantification.key_assumption: Onboarding lift is causally responsible for the H2 engagement gap. A/B test required to convert MEDIUM → HIGH confidence.

impact_quantification.opportunity_estimate: Re-introducing a softer first-month tier (or grandfathering Q3 signups) would reverse ~70% of the residual spike — ~340 churned users / quarter.
impact_quantification.key_assumption: The price perception effect, not the absolute price, is the driver. A targeted offer test would discriminate between hypotheses.

impact_quantification.opportunity_estimate: Per +10pp lift in first-feature reach, voluntary churn drops ~2.5pp (from H2 odds ratio). Bringing voluntary-churn cohort from 38% → 60% would cut their 90-day churn by ~5.5pp.
impact_quantification.key_assumption: H2's logistic relationship extrapolates linearly in the relevant range — supported by the within-tier replication.

insight_ranking.insight: Paid_search users (especially Google non-brand) churn voluntarily because the generic onboarding flow does not match their search intent — an intent-segmented onboarding test is the highest-leverage Q4 intervention.

The 2025-07-15 pricing change drove a Starter-tier-specific churn spike (+68% residual). Pricing-perception mitigation should be scoped narrowly to entry-tier first-bill experience, not the whole base.
First-feature activation is the single highest-leverage product fix: every 10-point lift in first_feature_used completion translates to a ~2.5pp drop in voluntary churn across the base.
